channel.title: PetSavings: Blog
channel.description: Practical pet advice for dog, cat and small pet owners: seasonal safety, reading food labels, new pet checklists and simple ways to save on pet costs.

item.title: Is my dog or cat overweight? A simple hands-on check you can do at home
item.description: How to tell if your dog or cat is overweight with a simple rib, waist and tummy check, why extra weight matters and how to start a plan with your vet.

item.title: Antifreeze poisoning in dogs and cats: the winter danger to know about
item.description: Antifreeze poisoning in dogs and cats: why ethylene glycol is so dangerous, signs to spot, what to do at once and how to keep pets safe this winter.

item.title: How to switch your dog's food without upsetting their tummy
item.description: How to change your dog's food without tummy upsets: a gradual 7 to 14 day plan from PDSA and Blue Cross, what to do if they refuse it and when to call a vet.

item.title: Pet food recalls: how to check, what to do and how to report a problem
item.description: Pet food recalls explained for US and UK owners: where to check official alerts, which batch details to keep, when to call the vet and how to report problems.

item.title: Pet insurance: pre-existing conditions and waiting periods explained
item.description: Pet insurance pre-existing conditions and waiting periods explained: what exclusions usually mean, what to check before you buy and how to compare policies.

item.title: Fireworks and pets: how to keep dogs and cats calm
item.description: How to prepare dogs, cats and small pets for fireworks season: safe dens, walk timing, noise, microchips and when to speak to your vet about anxiety.

item.title: How to read pet food labels
item.description: What dog and cat food labels really tell you: complete vs complementary, AAFCO statements, ingredient lists, “with chicken” naming rules and feeding guides.

item.title: New puppy checklist: what to buy and what to arrange
item.description: A complete new puppy checklist: the supplies to buy before day one, plus vet registration, vaccinations, microchip details, insurance and early training.

item.title: Winter and Christmas hazards for pets
item.description: The winter and holiday hazards most likely to harm pets: antifreeze, chocolate, grapes and raisins, xylitol, lilies, decorations and road salt, and what to do.
